solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Friends? Yes it completely showcases the six characters (6)

indicatorNotes.showcases: to showcase is to put on display, and the phrase displays the answer inside itself

blocks.note: yeS IT COMpletely: six letters run across the word breaks
surface padding that also tells you the hidden run is six letters long

annotation.surface: A fan insists the whole cast of Friends, all six of them, is showcased in full.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The six characters' reads as the six friends of the show, and it quietly tells you the hidden answer is six letters long. The question mark flags Friends as an example.
annotation.definitionFit: Friends is a famous American situation comedy, so a sitcom by example.

entries.clue: Symbolically significant style of architecture including Corinth’s capital (6)

indicatorNotes.including: the style takes the letter inside it
indicatorNotes.capital: a capital is the top of a column, and in a word the top is its first letter

blocks.note: the Ionic order of classical columns
first letter of Corinth, placed after the I

annotation.surface: An architecture lecture on a meaningful style that incorporates the capital of a Corinthian column.
annotation.walkthrough: Corinthian and Ionic are both column orders, so 'capital' sounds like the carved top of a column; here it just means Corinth's first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Something iconic carries weight as a symbol.

entries.clue: Made amends for hoax filled with funny pet names (11)

indicatorNotes.filled with: the hoax word has the rest put inside it
indicatorNotes.funny: funny as in odd: the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: cod, a hoax or sham, opened up to hold the rest: CO…D
PET NAMES rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone apologised for a prank that was stuffed with silly nicknames.
annotation.walkthrough: COD for a hoax is British slang (a cod accent is a fake one). 'Made amends for' fits the past tense of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to compensate for a loss or wrong is to make up for it.

entries.clue: Solo second number on spoken record (9)

indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, on means placed after
indicatorNotes.spoken: said aloud, so a word that sounds like record

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, a second
No. is short for number
a log is a record; LOGUE is pronounced the same

annotation.surface: A music listing: a solo, the second track on a spoken-word record.
annotation.walkthrough: Every word is a music term, so 'number' looks like a track; it is just the abbreviation NO.
annotation.definitionFit: A monologue is a speech by one performer alone, a solo.

entries.clue: Bottom is supporting fish (8)

blocks.note: backs = is supporting
the ide, a freshwater fish

annotation.surface: Bottom, the weaver in A Midsummer Night's Dream, is backing a fish.
annotation.walkthrough: Bottom, capitalised at the start, looks like Shakespeare's weaver; it is the ordinary word for the seat. IDE is a crossword regular among fish.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the part you sit on, the more polite word of the pair.

entries.clue: Carried right into branch on top of tree (7)

indicatorNotes.on top of: the top of tree is its first letter

blocks.note: a bough is a large branch; R sits inside: B(R)OUGH
R = right
first letter of tree

annotation.surface: Someone lugged something right up into the branches at the top of a tree.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Carried' is the past tense to match the answer, not a description of the climbing.
annotation.definitionFit: Brought is the past tense of bring, which is carrying something to a place.

entries.clue: Chap with name for charming women (5)

annotation.definitionNote: a coven is a single group, standing for the women in it

blocks.note: cove, old British slang for a chap
N = name

annotation.surface: A man with a reputation for women he finds charming.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Charming' means casting charms, spells, so the women are witches, not delightful company.
annotation.definitionFit: A coven is a gathering of witches, women who work charms.

entries.clue: Exclusive group write puzzles like this (3)

blocks.note: a clique of the fashionable, as in 'the jet' one
what a crossword compiler does to a puzzle

annotation.surface: A clique of insiders who write crosswords like the one you are solving.
annotation.walkthrough: The second definition points at the puzzle in front of you: a crossword compiler is called a setter.
annotation.definitionFit: A set is a closed social circle; to set a crossword is to compose it.

entries.clue: Laughing at key part of Yorkshire? (8)

blocks.note: D, a musical key
the East Riding, one of Yorkshire's historic divisions, written E RIDING

annotation.surface: Someone mocks a central piece of Yorkshire.
annotation.walkthrough: Yorkshire, a large county in northern England, was split into three Ridings; the East Riding survives in the name of a modern county area.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to deride is to mock, to laugh at with scorn.

entries.clue: Soldier married mother in New York apartment (8)

indicatorNotes.in: married and mother go inside the apartment

blocks.note: a condo, American for an owned flat; the rest goes inside CO…NDO
M = married
ma = mother

annotation.surface: A soldier who married, with his mother living in a New York flat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'New York' points to the American word CONDO rather than flat.
annotation.definitionFit: A soldier from a unit trained for raids, such as the Royal Marines commandos.

entries.clue: Enthusiastic follower’s reorder includes books (6)

indicatorNotes.includes: the reorder word takes the books inside

blocks.note: to vary is to change the order of things: V…ARY
OT, the Old Testament books

annotation.surface: A keen fan's rearranged shelf now takes in some books.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Reorder' looks like an anagram instruction, but no letters here are shuffled; it is the word VARY. The 's is 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A votary is a devoted follower of a cause or person.

entries.clue: Left alien tumbling in unbroken descent (6)

indicatorNotes.tumbling: the letters of alien fall into a new order

blocks.note: L = left
ALIEN rearranged

annotation.surface: An alien left behind, tumbling down in one continuous fall.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Descent' reads as a fall through the air; here it is family descent, a line of ancestry.
annotation.definitionFit: Lineal describes descent in a direct, unbroken line from an ancestor.

entries.clue: Serving boy returning regularly readies one’s horse (8)

indicatorNotes.returning: going back: the whole string is written backwards
indicatorNotes.regularly: something done regularly happens at even intervals, so take letters at even spacing

blocks.note: the even letters of rEaDiEs
one's = my, the possessive of a speaker
a nag, an old horse

annotation.surface: A stable boy comes back and, at regular times, gets a horse ready.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole string EDE+MY+NAG is written backwards. Ganymede was the Trojan youth carried off to be cupbearer to the Greek gods, hence 'serving boy'.
annotation.definitionFit: In myth Ganymede served wine to Zeus and the gods on Olympus.

entries.clue: Note girl is bourgeois (6-5)

blocks.note: middle C, the note at the centre of a piano keyboard
lass = girl

annotation.surface: A remark that some girl is conventional and suburban.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Note' looks like a jotted message; it is a musical note, and a whole six letters of it.
annotation.definitionFit: Bourgeois means belonging to, or having the values of, the middle class.

entries.clue: Sound weary walking along and playing straight off (5-7)

blocks.note: a sigh is the sound a tired person makes
treading = walking

annotation.surface: A tired musician trudges along while playing a piece without rehearsal.
annotation.walkthrough: The break in the answer falls in a different place from the break in the wordplay: SIGH plus TREADING, read as SIGHT plus READING.
annotation.definitionFit: Sight-reading is playing music at first sight, straight off the page.

entries.clue: What may serve up anisette with starter of moules? (9)

annotation.definition: What may serve up anisette with starter of moules?

indicatorNotes.up: served up, dished out in a new arrangement

blocks.note: anagram fodder
first letter of moules, added to the fodder
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A menu question: what sort of place brings you an aniseed drink alongside a first course of mussels?
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition as well as the wordplay: a French café-bar is just where you would get anisette and moules. 'Starter' is a menu pun on first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: An estaminet is a small French café or bar serving drinks and simple food.

entries.clue: Large gold crown is awarded to such a poet (8)

annotation.definition: crown is awarded to such a poet

blocks.note: L = large
aureate means golden

annotation.surface: A big golden crown handed to a certain kind of poet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gold crown' reads as one object, but the crown belongs to the definition: a laureate is one crowned with laurel.
annotation.definitionFit: Laureate describes a poet honoured with the laurel crown, as the Poet Laureate is.

entries.clue: Head waiter had title more involved (6,6)

indicatorNotes.more involved: more complicated: the letters are tangled

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A head waiter who once held a title became more deeply involved.
annotation.walkthrough: 'More' does double duty only in the surface; its letters are fodder, and 'involved' is the instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: The maître d'hôtel is the head waiter of a restaurant.

entries.clue: Postponing 100 in fast vehicle one may end up in a stew (7)

annotation.definition: one may end up in a stew

indicatorNotes.Postponing: the C is put off until later in the word

blocks.note: a racing chariot; its C is taken from the front: HARI…OT
C = 100 in Roman numerals, moved later into the word

annotation.surface: Delaying a hundred on a fast ride, someone might end up in hot water.
annotation.walkthrough: 'End up in a stew' sounds like getting into trouble; a haricot bean really does end up in a stew.
annotation.definitionFit: A haricot is a bean often cooked in stews, and also a mutton stew itself.

entries.clue: Food for livestock during season (6)

blocks.note: as in 'for a year' = during a year
an age, a period of time

annotation.surface: Farm animals' feed during a particular season.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a plain farming phrase, so the split after 'livestock' is the whole challenge.
annotation.definitionFit: Forage is fodder, the grass and hay that livestock eat.

entries.clue: One expecting payment from Times office after first pair of crosswords (8)

indicatorNotes.after: the office comes after the two letters
indicatorNotes.first pair of: the first two letters of crosswords

blocks.note: the first two letters of crosswords
the editor, a post at the Times

annotation.surface: Someone at the Times crossword desk waiting to be paid for a couple of puzzles.
annotation.walkthrough: An 'office' here is a post someone holds, not a room: the editorship.
annotation.definitionFit: A creditor is owed money and expects to be paid.

entries.clue: Perhaps keep in drawer (5)

blocks.note: a keep is the strong central building of a castle, given by example
one who tows, draws along

annotation.surface: Maybe store it in a drawer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drawer' looks like furniture, but it is one who draws, as a tug or tractor does, rhyming with 'lower'.
annotation.definitionFit: A keep is a fortress tower; a tower is also anything that tows.

entries.clue: Sign of extension for president (6)

blocks.note: the bar over a vowel marking it long
the surname of Emmanuel, president of France since 2017

annotation.surface: A signal that the president's term will be extended.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Extension' sounds political, a longer term in office; the sign marks a vowel as long.
annotation.definitionFit: A macron is the line over a vowel, as in ā, showing it is lengthened.

entries.clue: Concern recalled about a perennial growth (6)

indicatorNotes.about: about in the sense of around: the reversed word goes round the A

blocks.note: WORRY backwards, opened to take the A: Y…RROW
the A itself

annotation.surface: A worry brought back to mind about something that keeps coming up every year.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Perennial growth' sounds like a recurring problem; it is a plant.
annotation.definitionFit: Yarrow is a perennial plant with flat heads of small white flowers.

entries.clue: Space reduced for indigenous Australian (3)

indicatorNotes.reduced: cut short: the last letter goes

blocks.note: ROOM with its last letter removed

annotation.surface: Less room made for Aboriginal Australians.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Indigenous Australian' looks like a person; it is a native animal, the kangaroo.
annotation.definitionFit: A roo, short for kangaroo, is native to Australia.

entries.clue: Moth caught flying in a barn (8)

indicatorNotes.flying: the letters take off into a new order

blocks.note: c = caught, the cricket scoring abbreviation
IN A BARN rearranged

annotation.surface: A moth is caught fluttering about inside a barn.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flying' suits a moth so well in the surface that it hides its job as the instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: The cinnabar is a red and black day-flying moth.

entries.clue: Politician’s protest about informer (8)

blocks.note: a demo, a demonstration
c. = circa, about
a rat is one who informs on others

annotation.surface: A politician protests about someone who leaked to the authorities.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like the word for a container; here it is simply C, short for circa.
annotation.definitionFit: A Democrat is a politician of the US Democratic Party, or any champion of democracy.

entries.clue: Class brooded over preferences (6)

blocks.note: a set, a class at school
a hen broods by sitting on her eggs

annotation.surface: A class moped over what they liked.
annotation.walkthrough: SET then SAT, and the whole run is turned over. 'Brooded over' looks like one phrase for worrying; 'over' belongs to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: what suits your taste is what you prefer.
